newsitem.title: sao tome and principe: Sao Tome misuses foreign aid, banker says.
newsitem.headline: Sao Tome misuses foreign aid, banker says.

text.p: A senior banker has criticised the government of the African twin island state of Sao Tome and Principe for mishandling foreign aid.

Marcus Stephan, head of a joint mission from the World Bank, International Monetary Fund and African Development Bank, told local reporters during a visit this week: "There is no seriousness here to confront the challenges of development."

Stephan said the economy had deteriorated because authorities had allocated funds inefficiently in a climate of political instability. "The country is not making efforts to cover its expenditure," he said.
Stephan urged Sao Tomean authorities to implement administrative reforms, improve tax collection and instil greater political stability.
President Miguel Trovoada named a new prime minister on Tuesday after the collapse of the islands' coalition government.

Trovoada named Raul Braganca, deputy leader of the Movement for the Liberation of Sao Tome and Principe/Social Democratic Party (MLSTP/PSD), to replace Armindo Vaz de Almeida as head of government after two months of political talks.

Sao Tome and Principe, a former Portuguese colony located 200 km (125 miles) off Gabon, is one of the poorest countries in the world and is heavily dependent on foreign aid. The islands' population is 127,000.

Sao Tome's public finances and inflation rate have deteriorated in recent months as it grappled with a series of strikes by health workers, teachers and civil servants. The islands' foreign debt is about $300 million, officials said.
